newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa trims losses but 900 still looming.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa trims losses but 900 still looming.

text.p: Long liquidation and origin sales, helped by sterling's stronger tone, forced London cocoa futures down to near their lows on Tuesday but industry bids underpinned the market.
"Sterling is $1.6710. That poured in origin activity," said one trader.
An earlier bout of offers which drove March cocoa to a morning low of 906 stg was linked to left-over liquidation by funds after a round of last-minute selling on Monday.
The benchmark March contract finished the day off its session low of 904 stg when it ended seven stg down at 906 stg a tonne.

But the ominious prospect of a test of the crucial 900 stg was still looming, traders said. This psychological support is just below the contract low of 903 stg set in November, which was also a seven-month low on a continuation basis.

"Once Dec is off the board, March is going to take Dec's price because whoever is going to take March will be dumped with rubbish cocoa," said the trader, referring to stacks of cocoa delivered in September that may fail re-grading for the London market.
Volume on the exchange totalled 6,307 lots including a large volume of AAs. On the switches, March/May traded from 20 to 22 stg, traders said.
Sterling hovered above $1.67 in late European afternoon deals compared with $1.6620 on Monday.
In the physical market, Ivory Coast was selling forward positions.

One trader said the daily Ivorian sales must have totalled 4,000-5,000 tonnes on Monday and Tuesday. He added that Nigeria seemed to have sold the whole crop for this season while Cameroon had little left to offer.
Ivory cocoa for January positions was offered at 35 stg under the March futures contract and bid at 40-45 stg under. February was offered at 20 stg under and bid at 25-30 under, traders said.
